Which statements about logistic regression are correct? A. The linear predictor is the logit. B. The fitted probability can be outside [0,1] for finite η. C. exp(β) is an odds ratio. D. Logistic coefficients are estimated by OLS by default.
items.explanation: A and C are true. The inverse-logit keeps fitted probabilities in (0,1), and coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood.

items.stem: Which statements about odds and probability are correct? A. Odds equal p/(1−p). B. Odds are always between zero and one. C. Odds ratio 2 means odds double. D. Odds ratio 2 means probability doubles.
items.explanation: A and C are true. Odds can exceed one, and doubling odds does not generally double probability.
